title: Signage development examples
slide_intent: Teach designers to place identifying marks, arrows and service information where they can be read on signs of very different sizes.
strategic_value: Kelham Island Museum can use the same blue field and white lettering at pedestrian and building scale while adapting the message to the location.
demonstration: A freestanding sign pairs the venue name and arrow with amenities. A large wall panel pairs the venue name and arrow with the circular museum seal.
practical_value: Put local amenities on the smaller sign where a visitor can stop and read them. Give the large identifier a shorter reading sequence.

content_islands.name: Pedestrian sign
content_islands.spec: Frame the blue sign within the industrial site. Stack the name above the arrow, then list the nearby amenities below.

content_islands.name: Wall identification
content_islands.spec: Use a narrower photograph beside the first. Show the circular seal above the large venue mark and directional arrow on the blue wall.
